title: The Death of the Curate
question: Today, can the curate bear his witness aloud?
light: grey daylight from a breached wall, coal-black shadows
palette: coal black, limewash grey-white, slate grey, burgundy red, copper brown, cold daylight grey

pantry_door.described: A narrow Victorian walk at a walking pace-in pantry seen through its open plank door from the dark scullery. Grey daylight falls in from the scullery behind the camera at the left and lays a pale wedge across the brick floor, throwing coal-black shadows to the right. Thick grey slate shelves on brick piers run at a walking pace around three limewashed walls at waist height, two deal shelves above on iron brackets. On the slate at the left an earthenware bread pan with two loaves; at the back a gauze meat cover; at the right two tin biscuit boxes. A small zinc vent high in the back wall is packed with earth. The plank door frame stands in the near foreground, its iron latch at the right, and bare brick floor fills the space between the door and the shelf, swept and grey in the wedge of light.
pantry_door.landmark: the grey slate shelf on brick piers
pantry_door.route: from the scullery threshold at the plank door into the pantry to the slate shelf at the back wall
pantry_door.geometry: The open plank door frames the picture: its jamb rises up the LEFT edge and its iron latch sits at the RIGHT edge at waist height, each the full height of the frame. The slate shelf crosses the CENTRE third as a grey band at waist height, the bread pan on its LEFT third the size of a head, the biscuit tins on its RIGHT third. The zinc vent sits small at TOP CENTRE in the back wall. The brick floor fills the BOTTOM third between the camera and the shelf, the pale wedge of daylight lying across it from the LEFT.
pantry_door.ambience: close muffled hush, two men's ragged breathing, grit sifting from cracked boards, distant metallic hammering from the pit

scullery_copper.described: The north-west corner of a dim Victorian scullery buried in a ruined villa. A brick-built wash copper rendered in limewash stands in the corner, waist high, with a round wooden lid and a small iron fire door at its base. Beside it at the left a stack of split firewood rises to hip height. At the right a tall deal cupboard stands with its door ajar, showing the last bottle of burgundy and two biscuit tins on its shelves. Grey York stone flags cover the floor; limewashed brick walls rise to cracked whitewashed boards low overhead. The one light source is grey daylight falling in from the kitchen doorway at the RIGHT of the room, out of frame; it rakes from right to left across the flags, lights the right flank of the copper and the cupboard door, and throws long coal-black shadows to the LEFT across the stone and up the firewood.
scullery_copper.landmark: the brick wash copper with its round wooden lid
scullery_copper.route: from the deal cupboard at the right across the flags to the wash copper in the corner
scullery_copper.geometry: The wash copper stands at the CENTRE, a third of the frame's height, its round wooden lid level with the middle of the frame. The firewood stack fills the LEFT third from the BOTTOM edge to half height. The tall deal cupboard stands along the RIGHT edge, the full height of the frame, its door ajar toward the centre. The stone flags fill the BOTTOM third in front of the copper. The two brick walls meet in a dark vertical seam above the copper at TOP CENTRE.
scullery_copper.ambience: muffled hush, a drip at the stone sink, distant clanking machinery in the pit beyond the walls

scullery_kitchen_door.described: A Victorian scullery three yards across seen from beside the brick wash copper, looking east toward the kitchen door. The planked kitchen door stands half open in the far wall, a grey rectangle of daylight beyond it falling in across the York stone flags toward the camera and casting coal-black shadows behind every edge. A meat chopper with a wooden handle and a broad steel blade hangs on a nail on the wall at the right of the doorframe. At the left a shallow brown stone sink under a window packed with earth, a black cast-iron pump with a long curved handle beside it. At the right two closed plank doors with iron latches. Cracked whitewashed ceiling boards sit low overhead; limewashed brick walls stand grey in the gloom.
scullery_kitchen_door.landmark: the half-open kitchen door with the meat chopper beside it
scullery_kitchen_door.route: from the wash copper beside the camera across the flags to the kitchen door in the far wall
scullery_kitchen_door.geometry: The kitchen doorway stands at the CENTRE of the far wall, a grey rectangle half the frame's height. The meat chopper hangs on the RIGHT third beside the doorframe at shoulder height, the size of a hand. The sink and pump stand along the LEFT edge, the pump handle a quarter of the frame's height. The two plank doors line the RIGHT edge. The stone flags fill the BOTTOM third between the camera and the doorway, the doorway light lying on them as a pale strip.
scullery_kitchen_door.ambience: muffled hush, a drip at the sink, distant clanking machinery and a faint hiss of steam from the pit

kitchen_breach.described: A small half-buried Victorian back kitchen about four yards across, seen from the scullery doorway. The far wall is broken in: fallen beams slant from the upper left corner down onto a heap of debris and broken plaster, and among them a triangular aperture two feet on a side opens at head height above the heaped debris. A shaft of bright outer sunlight falls through the aperture from the far wall toward the camera, laying a bright triangle on the debris and the kitchen floor, dust hanging in it, every corner around it coal-black. Plaster walls stand in shadow at the left and right. The kitchen floor is strewn with fallen plaster and debris; laths show through the ceiling. The dark scullery doorframe stands at the near right. Grey daylight through the doorway at the LEFT, deep shadow.
kitchen_breach.landmark: the triangular aperture among the fallen beams
kitchen_breach.route: from the scullery doorway across the kitchen floor to the heaped debris under the triangular aperture
kitchen_breach.geometry: The triangular aperture sits at the CENTRE of the far wall in the TOP half, a bright patch a sixth of the frame's width, the fallen beams slanting from the TOP LEFT corner down to it. The heaped debris rises beneath the aperture across the CENTRE third. A shadowed plaster wall runs at a walking pace up the LEFT edge, the full height of the frame. The dark scullery doorframe cuts the RIGHT edge in the foreground. The kitchen floor fills the BOTTOM third, the sunlit triangle lying on it at the centre, half the width of the frame.
kitchen_breach.ambience: dust settling, plaster trickling down the debris, a heavy mechanical hum and clanking just beyond the broken wall

coal_cellar.described: A tiny low brick coal cellar one and a half yards square, a step below the scullery. A heap of black coal lumps rises against the back wall and split firewood lies stacked along the left side wall. Rough limewashed brick walls are furred with black coal dust, and a low vaulted brick ceiling sits close overhead. The plank door with an iron latch stands at the top of one brick step, and a thin line of grey daylight leaks in around its edges from the scullery beyond, falling forward across the coal and leaving the corners coal-black. Fine black dust coats every surface, and a few lumps of coal lie scattered on the step. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT, deep shadow.
coal_cellar.landmark: the plank door with its iron latch
coal_cellar.route: from the plank door down one brick step to the coal heap against the back wall
coal_cellar.geometry: The camera sits low on the coal heap looking back at the door. The plank door stands at the CENTRE, two thirds of the frame's height, its iron latch on the RIGHT third at mid-height, its edges outlined by the thin grey line of light. The brick step crosses the BOTTOM third below the door. Coal lumps fill the BOTTOM edge in the foreground, each the size of a fist. Split firewood rises up the LEFT edge from the bottom corner to half height. The vaulted brick ceiling closes over the TOP edge.
coal_cellar.ambience: dense coal-dust hush, a man's held breath, a faint metallic jingle like keys on a ring beyond the door

shots.frame: Medium at the open pantry door: the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) at the LEFT tipping a dark burgundy bottle to his mouth, and the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) at the RIGHT seizing the bottle by its neck.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the burgundy bottle a hand's breadth across the whole shot; the narrator wrenches the bottle by its neck; the curate twists and pulls it back against his chest, both men swaying against the doorframe.
shots.camera: In the dark scullery two yards outside the pantry door, at chest height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the LEFT behind the camera.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the dark burgundy bottle tilted at the curate's mouth in the LEFT third, his hand round its base. The narrator stands in the RIGHT third, his reaching hand at the bottle's neck. The grey slate shelf crosses the CENTRE behind them, the bread pan small on its left, the biscuit tins on its right half.
shots.end: The two men grapple at the CENTRE of the doorway, the burgundy bottle raised between their four hands, the slate shelf behind them, the curate's shoulder against the LEFT jamb, the narrator's boots braced on the brick floor at the RIGHT.

sounds.sound: two men scuffling on a brick floor

source: In the darkness I heard the curate drinking. I snatched in the darkness, and my fingers caught a bottle of burgundy.
shots.turn: secret drinking -> open struggle
shots.why: The hook: the curate has broken into the shared store, and the narrator stops him by force.

shots.frame: Medium close of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) in the pantry doorway, hugging the dark burgundy bottle to his chest and twisting away toward the LEFT jamb.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the curate's face across to the burgundy bottle at his chest a hand's breadth across the whole shot; the curate hugs the bottle tighter and twists his shoulder against the LEFT jamb at a normal pace; his head shakes from side to side as his fingers tighten on the bottle.
shots.camera: In the dark scullery a yard and a half outside the pantry door, at chest height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the LEFT behind the camera.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's face in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height, his pale blue eyes staring wide. The dark burgundy bottle is clasped to his chest at the CENTRE in both hands. The LEFT door jamb stands grey at the LEFT edge; the grey slate shelf with the biscuit tins crosses behind him in the RIGHT half.
shots.end: The burgundy bottle sits at the CENTRE clutched against the curate's black clerical waistcoat, his face in the TOP LEFT turned toward the jamb, his shoulder pressed to the LEFT jamb, the slate shelf and biscuit tins in the RIGHT half.

sounds.sound: two men scuffling on a brick floor

source: For a few minutes there was a tussle.
shots.turn: a secret drink -> a bottle fought over
shots.why: The curate clings to the drink he stole; the narrator's grip is about to cost them both.

shots.frame: Insert of the brick pantry floor where the burgundy bottle lies smashed, dark red wine spreading from the shards toward the brick pier under the slate shelf.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the broken neck of the burgundy; the dark red wine spreads between the bricks toward the brick pier; the pool keeps spreading between the mortar lines.
shots.camera: Low over the brick floor just inside the pantry door, a 35mm lens looking down; grey daylight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the broken neck of the burgundy bottle at the CENTRE of the brick floor, dark green shards around it in a ring. A pool of dark red wine spreads toward the BOTTOM edge. The foot of a brick pier under the grey slate shelf stands along the TOP edge, the LEFT door jamb grey in the corner, the pale wedge of daylight lying across the bricks from the LEFT.
shots.end: A wide dark red pool covers the CENTRE of the brick floor around the broken bottle neck, its edge touching the brick pier along the TOP edge, shards glinting in the LEFT third.

sounds.sound: a wine bottle smashing on a brick floor

source: The bottle struck the floor and broke, and I desisted and rose.
shots.turn: a full bottle -> wine lost on the floor
shots.why: The struggle costs them the drink; the narrator stops fighting and rises.

shots.frame: One single picture fills the whole frame edge to edge. Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) planted in the pantry doorway with his back to the slate shelf, his arms spread from jamb to jamb, his chest heaving.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator standing at the CENTRE; the narrator draws a long breath and squares his shoulders at a normal pace; he turns his head toward the scullery at the RIGHT, his chest rising and falling hard.
shots.camera: In the scullery two yards from the door at eye height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the LEFT behind the camera.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator standing at the CENTRE of the doorway, his head a quarter of the frame's height, one hand flat on each jamb at the LEFT and RIGHT edges. The slate shelf with the bread pan and biscuit tins runs at a walking pace behind his waist; the wine pool darkens the brick floor at the BOTTOM edge.
shots.end: The narrator stands squared in the doorway at the CENTRE, head turned to the RIGHT, hands gripping both jambs, the slate shelf behind his waist, the dark wine pool at his boots along the BOTTOM edge.
source: In the end I planted myself between him and the food, and told him of my determination to begin a discipline.
shots.turn: a man who shares -> a man who rules the food
shots.why: The narrator chooses discipline and guards the store with his own body.

shots.frame: One single picture fills the whole frame edge to edge. Close of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) in the pantry doorway, his face set hard, the slate shelf of food behind him.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the narrator's face a hand's breadth across the whole shot, looking down over his head to the bread pan on the slate shelf; the narrator's jaw sets and his head turns toward the scullery at the RIGHT at a normal pace; his chest rises and falls hard under the striped flannel.
shots.camera: In the scullery a yard from the door at eye height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the LEFT behind the camera.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, his grey eyes fixed toward the RIGHT. His dusty shoulders fill the BOTTOM edge; the grey slate shelf with the earthenware bread pan crosses behind his LEFT shoulder; the dark doorframe edges the RIGHT side of the frame.
shots.end: Seen from a little above, the narrator's face sits in the BOTTOM half, eyes turned to the RIGHT, the slate shelf with the bread pan spread across the TOP half behind him, the doorframe at the RIGHT edge.
source: I would not let him eat any more that day.
shots.turn: a guard at the door -> a judge of the food
shots.why: Seen close, the narrator's resolve hardens: the food behind him is his to ration.

shots.frame: Every surface in the picture is plain, wordless paint. Insert of ten small equal piles of food set in a row on the grey slate shelf of the pantry.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right a hand's breadth across the whole shot, past the bread pan, along the row of ration piles; grey daylight slides over the slate from the left; fine plaster grit sifts down from the deal shelf onto the piles.
shots.camera: Close over the slate shelf at waist height, a 50mm lens looking along the row; grey daylight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the first ration pile in the LEFT third of the slate, a small heap of torn bread. The other piles stand in a line toward the RIGHT edge. The earthenware bread pan stands in the TOP LEFT corner, a gauze meat cover at the TOP edge against the limewashed brick.
shots.end: The last ration piles fill the RIGHT third of the slate, a tin biscuit box beyond them at the RIGHT edge, the bread pan passed out at the LEFT edge, grit dusting the CENTRE piles.
source: I divided the food in the pantry, into rations to last us ten days.
shots.turn: food eaten freely -> ten days counted out
shots.why: The narrator's discipline made visible: ten piles, one a day.

shots.frame: Full of the two men sitting on the stone flags face to face beside the wash copper: the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) slumped against the copper at the LEFT, the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) upright against the deal cupboard at the RIGHT.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the copper lid a hand's breadth across the whole shot, widening to show the firewood stack, the copper and the deal cupboard; the curate rocks against the brick of the copper and wipes his face with his hand; the narrator's head drops forward onto his knees and lifts again, his shoulders jerking upright.
shots.camera: On the flags three yards from the copper at seated eye height, a 35mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the round wooden lid of the copper at the CENTRE, the curate's head beside it in the LEFT third. The narrator sits in the RIGHT third against the cupboard door, his knees drawn up. The firewood stack fills the LEFT edge; the stone flags fill the BOTTOM third between them.
shots.end: The curate slumps against the copper in the LEFT third, the narrator sits against the cupboard in the RIGHT third, the firewood stack stands at the LEFT edge, the stone flags lie across the BOTTOM third, the wall seam rises at TOP CENTRE.
source: All day and all night we sat face to face, I weary but resolute, and he weeping and complaining of his immediate hunger.
shots.turn: a quarrel -> an endless siege of hunger
shots.why: Time stretches: a day and a night face to face, the narrator weary but resolute.

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) sitting against the deal cupboard with his knees drawn up, fighting sleep in the dark scullery.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator's face a thumb's width across the whole shot; the narrator's head drops forward onto his knees and jerks upright again; his head sags forward toward his knees once more, his shoulders rounding.
shots.camera: On the flags two yards from the cupboard at seated eye height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his chin sinking toward his drawn-up knees. The ajar door of the deal cupboard stands behind his RIGHT shoulder, the last bottle of burgundy on its shelf; the grey flags fill the BOTTOM edge; faint grey light falls across his face from the RIGHT.
shots.end: The narrator sits at the CENTRE, his head a quarter of the frame's height, sagging toward his knees in the BOTTOM third, the cupboard door dark behind his RIGHT shoulder, the flags along the BOTTOM edge.
source: In the afternoon he made a feeble effort to get at the food. I had been dozing, but in an instant I was awake.
shots.turn: resolve -> exhaustion held off by force
shots.why: The cost of guarding the food: the narrator fights his own sleep to keep the watch.

shots.frame: Insert of the last dark burgundy bottle standing on a shelf of the deal cupboard, its door ajar, two biscuit tins on the shelf below it.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the biscuit tins to the burgundy bottle, travelling a hand's breadth, across the whole shot; the grey light from the doorway slides along the bottle's dark glass; fine plaster grit sifts down from the cracked ceiling boards across the bottle's shoulder.
shots.camera: Close in front of the deal cupboard at shoulder height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the two biscuit tins on the lower shelf of the deal cupboard in the BOTTOM half. The last dark burgundy bottle stands on the shelf above at the CENTRE of the TOP half, its cork pale. The ajar cupboard door cuts the RIGHT edge; limewashed brick shows at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The burgundy bottle fills the CENTRE, grey light along its dark glass at the RIGHT, plaster grit lying on its shoulder, the tops of the biscuit tins cut by the BOTTOM edge, the cupboard door at the RIGHT edge.
source: once I tried to bribe him with the last bottle of burgundy
shots.turn: a shared store -> the last bottle kept as a bribe
shots.why: What the narrator still holds back while the curate weeps: the last burgundy, kept as a bargain.

shots.frame: Medium of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) hunched against the wash copper, babbling to himself, one hand reaching toward the deal cupboard.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the curate a hand's breadth across the whole shot; the curate rocks forward and back against the copper, babbling to himself; his hand reaches out toward the cupboard at the RIGHT.
shots.camera: Beside the firewood stack at seated eye height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate hunched at the CENTRE against the limewashed copper, his head a quarter of the frame's height. The split firewood fills the LEFT third in the foreground; the copper's small iron fire door sits low at the BOTTOM edge; the deal cupboard door stands ajar at the RIGHT edge, the biscuit tins dark on its shelves.
shots.end: The curate fills the CENTRE of the frame against the copper, his head turned to the RIGHT toward the cupboard, the firewood a dark strip at the LEFT edge, his hand stretched out toward the BOTTOM RIGHT.
source: He would neither desist from his attacks on the food nor from his noisy babbling to himself.
Slowly I began to realise the complete overthrow of his intelligence, to perceive that my sole companion in this close and sickly darkness was a man insane.
shots.turn: a hungry companion -> a man insane
shots.why: The narrator perceives the overthrow of the curate's mind; the danger now sits beside him.

shots.frame: Medium of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) sitting in the darkness near the wash copper, talking aloud to himself, his face lifting toward the ceiling boards.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the copper, travelling two strides at a walking pace, across the whole shot; the curate rocks against the copper, talking aloud; his face lifts toward the ceiling boards as his voice keeps rising.
shots.camera: Beside the firewood stack at seated eye height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate sitting at the CENTRE against the limewashed copper, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his mouth open in speech. The split firewood fills the LEFT third in the foreground; the copper's small iron fire door sits low at the BOTTOM edge; the deal cupboard door stands ajar at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The curate sits small at the CENTRE of the frame against the copper, his face lifted toward the TOP edge, the firewood a dark strip at the LEFT edge, the cupboard door at the RIGHT edge, the stone flags across the BOTTOM third.
source: On the eighth day he began to talk aloud instead of whispering
shots.turn: whispering -> talking aloud
shots.why: The curate's voice leaves the whisper behind; the narrator can no longer moderate it.

shots.frame: Medium close of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) sitting in the darkness against the wash copper, face lifted to the ceiling boards, crying out aloud to God.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the curate cries out to the ceiling, his open hands lifting in front of him; his head rocks back and forth as his voice rises.
shots.camera: On the flags a yard and a half from the copper at seated eye height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, tipped up toward the TOP edge as he sits against the copper. The round wooden lid of the copper sits behind his LEFT shoulder; the cracked whitewashed boards run at a walking pace along the TOP edge; the firewood is a dark mass at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The curate's face fills the CENTRE, head bowed forward, tears on his cheeks, his open hands lifted at the BOTTOM edge, the copper lid behind his LEFT shoulder, the ceiling boards along the TOP edge.
source: It is just, O God!
We have sinned, we have fallen short.
shots.turn: whispering -> talking aloud
shots.why: The curate's guilt breaks into speech, and the narrator cannot quiet it.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) leaning forward from the deal cupboard, one hand raised, imploring across the dark scullery.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator's face a thumb's width across the whole shot; the narrator leans forward and implores, his raised palm pressing toward the left of frame; his head tips back toward the ceiling boards, listening for the pit.
shots.camera: On the flags a yard and a half from the cupboard at seated eye height, a 50mm lens; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his raised palm in the LEFT third. The ajar door of the deal cupboard stands behind his RIGHT shoulder, the last bottle of burgundy dark on its shelf; the grey flags fill the BOTTOM edge.
shots.end: The narrator's face fills the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, tipped back toward the TOP edge, the raised palm at the LEFT edge, the cupboard door dark behind his RIGHT shoulder.
source: he threatened he would shout and bring the Martians upon us.
Be still!
shots.turn: pleading -> fear of the pit
shots.why: The narrator's fear: any noise will bring the Martians upon them.

shots.frame: Medium close of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) rising from the flags to his knees beside the wash copper, declaring aloud.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from his chest, travelling a forearm, across the whole shot; the curate rises onto his knees and throws his head back; his mouth opens wide as his shoulders lift and his voice swells toward the ceiling.
shots.camera: Low on the flags a yard from the copper, a 50mm lens aimed at his chest; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's chest and black clerical waistcoat at the CENTRE, his face in the TOP third, his head a third of the frame's height. The copper's iron fire door sits at the BOTTOM LEFT; the round wooden lid is level with his shoulders at the LEFT edge; the cupboard is a dark band at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The curate kneels upright at the CENTRE, his face filling the TOP half, head half the frame's height, his mouth wide, the copper lid below his LEFT elbow, the ceiling boards across the TOP edge.
source: He rose to his knees, for he had been sitting in the darkness near the copper.
and now I must bear my witness.
shots.turn: silence kept -> witness proclaimed
shots.why: The curate chooses to speak loud enough for the pit; his question opens.

shots.frame: Medium close of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) kneeling upright beside the wash copper, declaring aloud.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the curate's waistcoat to his face, travelling a hand's breadth, across the whole shot; the curate throws his head back on his knees; his shoulders lift as his voice swells toward the ceiling.
shots.camera: Low on the flags a yard from the copper, a 50mm lens aimed at his chest; faint grey daylight comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's chest and black clerical waistcoat at the CENTRE, his face in the TOP third, his head a third of the frame's height. The copper's iron fire door sits at the BOTTOM LEFT; the round wooden lid is level with his shoulders at the LEFT edge; the cupboard is a dark band at the RIGHT edge.
shots.end: The curate kneels upright at the CENTRE, his face filling the TOP half, head half the frame's height, his mouth wide, the copper lid below his LEFT elbow, the ceiling boards across the TOP edge.
source: I have been still too long,” he said, in a tone that must have reached the pit, “and now I must bear my witness.
shots.turn: silence kept -> witness proclaimed
shots.why: The curate chooses to speak loud enough for the pit; his question opens.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) springing to his feet before the half-open kitchen door, hissing across the scullery.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the narrator rises from a crouch to his full height and thrusts one hand out; he hisses the words, his head and shoulders jerking round toward the kitchen doorway.
shots.camera: Beside the wash copper at standing eye height, two yards from him, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway behind him at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height, backlit by the grey doorway. The half-open kitchen door makes a grey rectangle at the CENTRE behind him; the meat chopper hangs on its nail in the RIGHT third at shoulder height.
shots.end: The narrator stands at full height in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height and turned toward the doorway, one hand thrust toward the camera, the grey doorway at the CENTRE behind him, the chopper on its nail in the RIGHT third.
source: rising to my feet, and in a terror lest the Martians should hear us.
shots.turn: imploring -> commanding in terror
shots.why: The narrator's terror becomes a command; he believes the Martians can hear.

shots.frame: Medium close over the shoulder and back of the head of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) toward the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open), who stands facing him with both arms flung wide, shouting.
shots.motion: The camera holds over the narrator's shoulder toward the curate across the whole shot; the curate flings his arms wider and shouts at the top of his voice; his head jerks round toward the kitchen doorway as his arms keep reaching.
shots.camera: Behind the narrator's right shoulder at standing eye height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway behind the curate at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his arms spread toward the LEFT and RIGHT edges. The narrator's shoulder and the back of his head fill the BOTTOM LEFT corner in the foreground. The grey rectangle of the kitchen doorway glows behind the curate's RIGHT shoulder.
shots.end: The curate stands at the CENTRE with his arms flung wide, his face turned to the RIGHT toward the grey doorway, the narrator's shoulder dark in the BOTTOM LEFT corner, the meat chopper on its nail at the RIGHT edge.
source: shouted the curate, at the top of his voice, standing likewise and extending his arms.
shots.turn: a quarrel in the dark -> a man going to the pit
shots.why: The curate declares the word of the Lord upon him and chooses to go.

shots.frame: Medium close of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) standing before the grey kitchen doorway with both arms flung wide, shouting at the top of his voice.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the curate flings his arms wider and shouts at the top of his voice; his head and shoulders swing round toward the kitchen doorway as his arms keep reaching.
shots.camera: Two yards in front of the curate at standing eye height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway behind him at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's face at the CENTRE, his head a third of the frame's height, his arms spread toward the LEFT and RIGHT edges. The grey rectangle of the kitchen doorway glows behind his RIGHT shoulder; the meat chopper hangs on its nail at the RIGHT edge; limewashed brick fills both TOP corners.
shots.end: The curate stands at the CENTRE with his arms flung wide, his head and shoulders turned to the RIGHT toward the grey doorway, the meat chopper on its nail at the RIGHT edge, limewashed brick in both TOP corners.
source: Speak! The word of the Lord is upon me!
shots.turn: a quarrel in the dark -> a man going to the pit
shots.why: The curate declares the word of the Lord upon him and chooses to go.

shots.frame: Medium behind the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) as he strides at a walking pace across the stone flags toward the half-open kitchen door, arms raised.
shots.motion: The camera tracks behind the curate as he walks at a walking pace toward the kitchen door, one stride at a walking pace across the whole shot, moving with him; the curate pushes the half-open door wide with his hand; he turns his head to cry back over his shoulder, his raised arms shaking in the doorway light.
shots.camera: Two yards behind the curate at shoulder height, moving with him, a 35mm lens; grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway ahead at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's back at the CENTRE, his matted curls and black clerical waistcoat dark against the grey doorway ahead, his arms raised. The meat chopper hangs on its nail at the RIGHT of the doorframe; the stone sink and pump stand at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The curate fills the CENTRE of the open doorway, his raised arms black against the grey kitchen light, his face turned back over his LEFT shoulder, the meat chopper on its nail at the RIGHT edge of the frame.
source: In three strides he was at the door leading into the kitchen.
I must bear my witness! I go! It has already been too long delayed.
shots.turn: kept in the scullery -> at the threshold
shots.why: Three strides, and the curate stands where the pit will hear him.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) beside the kitchen doorframe, his hand closing on the wooden handle of the meat chopper on its nail.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the narrator's face across to the meat chopper on its nail a hand's breadth across the whole shot; the narrator's hand closes on the wooden handle and lifts the chopper off the nail; he turns the broad blade back in his grip as he swings toward the doorway.
shots.camera: Beside the plank doors at the right wall, a yard from him at shoulder height, a 50mm lens; grey daylight comes from the kitchen doorway at the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face in the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height, his eyes on the doorway. The meat chopper hangs on its nail in the RIGHT third, its broad steel blade grey against the limewash. The edge of the grey doorway cuts the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The narrator's fist grips the chopper handle at the CENTRE, the blade turned back toward his wrist, the empty nail on the limewash in the RIGHT third, his shoulder moving into the grey doorway light at the LEFT edge.
source: I put out my hand and felt the meat chopper hanging to the wall. In a flash I was after him.
shots.turn: unarmed -> armed with the chopper
shots.why: The narrator chooses violence, yet turns the blade back: one last touch of humanity.

shots.frame: Full of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) overtaking the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) halfway across the kitchen and striking his head with the butt of the meat chopper.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the kitchen floor to the triangular aperture, travelling two strides at a walking pace, across the whole shot; the narrator swings the butt of the chopper down onto the curate's head; the curate pitches headlong forward and lies stretched on the ground, plaster grit skittering across the floor around him.
shots.camera: In the scullery doorway at chest height, four yards back, a 35mm lens; bright sunlight comes from the triangular aperture in the far wall at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate at the CENTRE of the kitchen, his arms raised toward the bright triangular aperture, his head a sixth of the frame's height. The narrator is one stride at a walking pace behind him in the LEFT third, the chopper raised butt-first. The sunlit triangle lies on the plaster-strewn kitchen floor in the BOTTOM half; the shadowed plaster wall stands at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The curate lies stretched face down across the sunlit triangle at the CENTRE, arms flung toward the heaped debris; the narrator stands over him in the LEFT third, the chopper hanging from his fist; the dark scullery doorframe cuts the RIGHT edge.

sounds.sound: a wooden chopper handle striking a skull, a dull thud
a body falling headlong onto a kitchen floor

source: Before he was halfway across the kitchen I had overtaken him.
With one last touch of humanity I turned the blade back and struck him with the butt. He went headlong forward and lay stretched on the ground.
shots.turn: the curate's witness going out -> silenced on the floor
shots.why: The turn: the curate's choice to cry out to the pit meets the narrator's blow; one man acts on the other.

shots.frame: Full of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) standing panting over the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open), who lies stretched face down on the kitchen floor, as plaster slides down the debris and the triangular aperture goes dark.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the two men a hand's breadth across the whole shot, looking down over the kitchen to the heaped debris; a stream of white plaster slips down the debris below the aperture; the grey metal underside of the Martian handling-machine, a metallic spider-crab of a machine, slides across the bright triangle, the light on the floor dimming to grey.
shots.camera: Three yards back at head height, a 35mm lens looking toward the far wall; sunlight comes from the triangular aperture at the TOP of the far wall.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate lying face down across the sunlit triangle at the CENTRE, his arms toward the debris. The narrator stands over him in the LEFT third, his head a fifth of the frame's height, the chopper hanging from his fist. The bright triangular aperture sits at TOP CENTRE above the heaped debris.
shots.end: Seen from above, the curate lies at the CENTRE on the grey-lit floor, the narrator in the LEFT third staring up, fresh white plaster heaped on the debris, the triangular aperture at TOP CENTRE filled by a dark metal underside.

sounds.sound: slipping plaster running and smashing down a heap of debris

source: Suddenly I heard a noise without, the run and smash of slipping plaster, and the triangular aperture in the wall was darkened.
shots.turn: silence won -> the pit has heard
shots.why: The cost of the shouting: the narrator has silenced him too late, and the machine comes.

shots.frame: Insert of the heaped debris beneath the triangular aperture, where a jointed gripping limb of the Martian handling-machine, a squat metal body on many jointed gripping limbs, curls amid the debris and fresh plaster.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the loose debris up to the fallen beams, travelling a hand's breadth, across the whole shot; the gripping limb curls amid the debris and pushes a lump of plaster down; a second jointed limb feels its way over the fallen beams, its metal joints flexing.
shots.camera: At the foot of the heaped debris, low at knee height, a 35mm lens looking up; sunlight comes from the aperture at the TOP edge.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the jointed grey metal gripping limb curled amid the debris at the CENTRE, fresh white plaster spilling round it. Loose debris fills the BOTTOM third; the end of one of the fallen beams crosses the TOP LEFT corner; a wedge of sunlight from the aperture falls across the TOP edge.
shots.end: The fallen beams cross the TOP half, a second jointed metal limb feeling over them at the TOP LEFT, the first limb curled amid the debris at the BOTTOM CENTRE, a loosened lump of plaster at the BOTTOM edge, sunlight across the TOP RIGHT.
source: I looked up and saw the lower surface of a handling-machine coming slowly across the hole. One of its gripping limbs curled amid the debris; another limb appeared, feeling its way over the fallen beams.
shots.turn: a dark hole -> a machine feeling inward
shots.why: The Martians answer the curate's shouting; the narrator stands petrified, staring.

shots.frame: Medium of the triangular aperture where the Martian handling-machine, a rounded grey-brown bulk with two immense dark eyes, peers through a glass plate at the edge of the Martian handling-machine's body while a long metallic tentacle feels through the opening into the kitchen.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; the jointed metallic tentacle lifts off the debris and snakes through the aperture into the kitchen, twisting this way and that; the machine's grey metal body tilts down across the aperture toward the room.
shots.camera: On the heaped debris two yards below the aperture at head height, a 50mm lens; sunlight comes from behind the machine at the TOP.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the glass plate at the CENTRE of the aperture, the two immense dark eyes of the Martian handling-machine behind it. The grey metal body of the Martian handling-machine fills the TOP half of the opening; the tip of a jointed metallic tentacle rests on the debris at the BOTTOM edge; a fallen beam crosses the TOP LEFT corner.
shots.end: The glass plate and the two dark eyes fill the TOP half at the CENTRE, the grey metal body tipped down toward the room, the metallic tentacle stretched down across the debris toward the BOTTOM RIGHT corner, its tip turning over the plaster, the beam across the TOP LEFT.

sounds.sound: a faint metallic ringing like keys on a split ring

source: and the large dark eyes of a Martian, peering, and then a long metallic snake of tentacle came feeling slowly through the hole.
I turned by an effort, stumbled over the curate, and stopped at the scullery door.
shots.turn: a machine outside -> the Martian looking in
shots.why: The eyes that heard the curate now search the room; the narrator stumbles back to the scullery.

shots.frame: Medium of the Martian handling-machine's metallic tentacle dragging the body of the curate (pale blue eyes, dog collar sprung open) across the floor of the kitchen toward the bright triangular aperture, while the Martian handling-machine's dark eyes peer down at his head.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the curate's head a stride at a walking pace across the whole shot, widening to show the whole broken wall and the Martian handling-machine in the aperture; the metallic tentacle drags the curate's body across the floor toward the opening; plaster grit scatters along the floor behind his trailing boots.
shots.camera: In the scullery doorway at crouching height, four yards back, a 50mm lens; bright sunlight comes from the triangular aperture at TOP CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's head at the CENTRE on the kitchen floor, his matted curls under a metallic tentacle tip. His body stretches toward the BOTTOM LEFT corner; the heaped debris rises in the TOP half; the grey bulk of the Martian handling-machine fills the triangular aperture at the TOP edge.
shots.end: The curate's body lies at the foot of the heaped debris at the CENTRE in the triangle of sunlight, the metallic tentacle tip at his head, the Martian handling-machine's grey bulk filling the triangular aperture at TOP CENTRE, the shadowed plaster wall at the LEFT edge, a drag mark across the floor in the BOTTOM third.

sounds.sound: a heavy body dragged across a kitchen floor

source: was dragged across the floor of the kitchen towards the opening.
In the triangle of bright outer sunlight I saw the Martian, in its Briareus of a handling-machine, scrutinizing the curate's head.
shots.turn: the curate's witness -> the pit takes him
shots.why: The answer: the curate is heard at last, by the Martians, and taken; the narrator fears the blow's mark will betray him.

shots.frame: Full of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) among the coal and firewood in the cellar, covering himself up with lumps of coal and split firewood.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the narrator a hand's breadth across the whole shot, looking down over the coal heap; the narrator lays split firewood over himself and settles deeper among the coal; his hands rake lumps of coal over his chest, black dust rising round him.
shots.camera: Above the coal heap close under the vaulted ceiling, a 28mm lens looking down; a thin grey line of light comes from the plank door edges at the TOP of frame.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator among the black coal at the CENTRE, his head a fifth of the frame's height, his arms full of split firewood. Coal lumps cover his boots at the BOTTOM edge; the firewood stack rises up the LEFT edge; the plank door outlined in grey light stands in the TOP third.
shots.end: From above, the narrator lies covered at the CENTRE under coal and firewood, his face and one hand showing, the firewood stack along the LEFT edge, the grey-lined plank door in the TOP third.
source: I crept back to the coal cellar, shut the door, and began to cover myself up as much as I could, and as noiselessly as possible in the darkness, among the firewood and coal therein.
shots.turn: a witness at the door -> a man hiding
shots.why: The narrator chooses to bury himself where the machine might reach.

shots.frame: Insert of the iron latch on the inside of the cellar's plank door as the Martian handling-machine's tentacle beyond the planks worries the catch up and down.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the iron latch at the CENTRE; the iron latch bar jerks up and drops back in its catch as the Martian handling-machine beyond the planks worries it; the bar lifts clear and the door swings open a hand's breadth, grey light widening across the step.
shots.camera: On the coal heap a yard from the door at latch height, a 50mm lens; a thin grey line of light comes from the door's edges at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the iron latch at the CENTRE of the planks, its bar resting in the catch. A thin grey line of light runs at a walking pace down the door's RIGHT edge; the brick step crosses the BOTTOM third with scattered coal lumps; coal dust furs the planks in the LEFT half.
shots.end: The plank door stands a hand's breadth open at the CENTRE, the latch bar raised, a band of grey light across the brick step in the BOTTOM third, the tip of a metallic Martian handling-machine tentacle in the gap at the RIGHT edge.

sounds.sound: an iron latch rattling in its catch

source: then I heard it fumbling at the latch! It had found the door! The Martians understood doors!
It worried at the catch for a minute, perhaps, and then the door opened.
shots.turn: a shut door -> the Martians understand doors
shots.why: The narrator's last wall fails; the machine has learned the latch.

shots.frame: Medium of the Martian handling-machine's long metallic tentacle reaching through the open cellar door, swaying its blind tip to and fro over the coal, the brick wall and the vaulted ceiling.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the door to the coal heap, travelling two strides at a walking pace, across the whole shot; the Martian handling-machine sways its tip over the brick wall and taps the vaulted ceiling; it lowers to the firewood and feels along the split logs, its joints ringing faintly.
shots.camera: Low on the coal heap two yards from the door, a 35mm lens; grey light comes through the open door at the CENTRE.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the jointed metallic Martian handling-machine tentacle entering through the open door at the CENTRE, its tip raised over the coal heap. The split firewood stack rises up the LEFT edge; the vaulted brick ceiling closes over the TOP edge; coal lumps the size of fists fill the BOTTOM edge.
shots.end: The metallic Martian handling-machine tentacle stretches from the TOP RIGHT across the frame, its tip pressed among the split logs in the LEFT third, the firewood stack along the LEFT edge, coal dust drifting in the grey light at the CENTRE.

sounds.sound: a faint metallic jingle like keys on a split ring

source: It was like a black worm swaying its blind head to and fro.
shots.turn: searching out there -> searching in here
shots.why: The blind search reaches the cellar, a yard from where the narrator lies.

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) covered among the coal and firewood, biting his own hand, while the metallic Martian handling-machine tip touches the heel of his boot at the edge of the coal.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the narrator's face, travelling a forearm, across the whole shot; the narrator bites hard into his own hand as the Martian handling-machine tip taps along his boot heel; his shoulders shake under the coal, his chest heaving against the lumps.
shots.camera: On the coal heap level with his face, two yards away, a 50mm lens; grey light comes from the open door at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE among black coal lumps, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his grey eyes wide. His hand is raised at his mouth in the LEFT third. The heel of his black boot juts from the coal at the RIGHT edge, the metallic Martian handling-machine tip touching it.
shots.end: Seen a quarter turn round, the narrator lies at the CENTRE, teeth sunk in his hand in the LEFT third, the Martian handling-machine tip lifted off his boot heel at the RIGHT edge, coal lumps across the BOTTOM edge.
source: Once, even, it touched the heel of my boot. I was on the verge of screaming; I bit my hand.
shots.turn: hidden -> touched
shots.why: The nearest he comes to discovery; the narrator bites his hand to hold the scream in.

shots.frame: Insert of the metallic Martian handling-machine's tip closing round a lump of coal on the heap and drawing it back toward the open door.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right a hand's breadth across the whole shot, past the split log, with the Martian handling-machine tip behind it; the tip clicks shut round the lump of coal and lifts it from the heap; the tentacle draws the lump toward the grey band of light, coal dust trailing from it.
shots.camera: Low on the coal heap at the level of the lumps, a 50mm lens; grey light comes from the open door at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS one fist-sized lump of coal at the CENTRE of the heap, the jointed Martian handling-machine tip curled over it. Coal lumps fill the BOTTOM half; a split log lies across the LEFT third; the grey band of light from the open door crosses the TOP RIGHT corner.
shots.end: A hollow in the coal heap sits at the CENTRE where the lump lay, the Martian handling-machine tip with the gripped lump in the TOP RIGHT in the grey light, the split log at the LEFT edge, dust drifting over the hollow.
source: Presently, with an abrupt click, it gripped something
Apparently it had taken a lump of coal to examine.
shots.turn: it has me -> it took coal
shots.why: The grip he took for his own arrest closes on a lump of coal; the narrator dares to breathe.

shots.frame: Medium of the cellar's plank door seen from the coal heap as the metallic Martian handling-machine beyond raps it shut and the grey light narrows to a line round its edges.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the brick step a hand's breadth across the whole shot, looking down at the door; the metallic Martian handling-machine beyond raps the door and swings it shut, the latch dropping into its catch; a heavy bump shakes the planks and coal dust sifts down from the lintel.
shots.camera: Low on the coal heap two and a half yards from the door, a 35mm lens; grey light comes through the door's gap at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the plank door at the CENTRE, two thirds of the frame's height, standing a hand's breadth open, a band of grey light in the gap at its RIGHT edge. The brick step crosses the BOTTOM third with scattered coal lumps on it; the iron latch sits in the RIGHT third; split firewood rises up the LEFT edge; the vaulted ceiling closes over the TOP edge.
shots.end: The plank door stands shut at the CENTRE, a thin grey line of light round its edges, the iron latch down in its catch in the RIGHT third, coal dust drifting in front of the planks, the firewood along the LEFT edge, the step dark along the BOTTOM edge.

sounds.sound: a sharp rap on a plank door
a glass bottle smashing on a brick floor
a heavy bump against a wooden door

source: it rapped smartly against the cellar door and closed it.
and the biscuit-tins rattled and a bottle smashed, and then came a heavy bump against the cellar door.
shots.turn: searched -> left in suspense
shots.why: The silence after the search; the narrator cannot tell whether it has gone.

shots.frame: Medium looking straight down on the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) lying buried among coal and firewood in the dark cellar, his face turned toward the shut door.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the narrator's face a thumb's width across the whole shot, widening to show the whole coal cellar and the shut door; the narrator's chest rises and falls under the firewood; the grey line of light round the door brightens and dims as the hours pass.
shots.camera: Above the coal heap two yards over his face, looking straight down on it, a 50mm lens; a thin grey line of light comes from the shut door at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE seen from above among the coal, his head a quarter of the frame's height, grey eyes open toward the door. Split firewood lies over his chest in the BOTTOM third; the shut door's thin grey outline sits in the TOP RIGHT corner; coal fills the LEFT edge.
shots.end: Seen from above, the whole cellar fills the frame: the narrator a buried shape on the coal heap in the BOTTOM half, the split firewood stack at the LEFT edge, the shut plank door outlined in grey at the CENTRE of the TOP half, the vaulted ceiling above.
source: but I lay all the tenth day in the close darkness, buried among coals and firewood
It was the eleventh day before I ventured so far from my security.
shots.turn: hiding for an hour -> buried for a day
shots.why: The world's answer: the narrator survives alone, buried and thirsting, until the eleventh day.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: On the sixth day, I heard the curate drinking in the dark.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: My hand found the bottle.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We wrestled until the bottle burst on the bricks.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I let go, panting.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I stood between him and the food, and told him a discipline began now.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Nothing more for him today.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I split what the pantry held into ten piles: ten days, if we kept to them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A night and a day we sat facing each other.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He wept with hunger; I fought off sleep.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: For two days I beat him, coaxed him, even bribed him with wine.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Neither force nor kindness reached him.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I understood: he was mad.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: By the eighth day he spoke aloud.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: It is just, O God! We have sinned, we have fallen short.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Be still!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He had threatened to cry out and call the Martians down on us.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He rose to his knees.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: I have been still too long, and now I must bear my witness.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Shut up! For God's sake!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I had sprung up, sick with fear of the pit.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He stood and threw his arms wide.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: Nay! Speak! The word of the Lord is upon me!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He cried out his witness, and three strides carried him to the kitchen door.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: My hand found the meat chopper on the wall.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Fear made me fierce.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Halfway across the kitchen I caught him, and struck him with the chopper's butt.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then plaster ran outside, and the hole went dark.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A handling machine slid across the gap. I stood frozen.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A Martian's dark eyes peered through glass. A tentacle came feeling in.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It dragged the curate toward the light and studied his head.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The pit had heard him.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I fled to the coal cellar and buried myself in coal.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Something fumbled at the latch.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The Martians understood doors.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It swayed over the coal like a blind black worm.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: It touched the heel of my boot.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I bit my hand.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A click. It had only taken a lump of coal.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I lay buried all the tenth day, and dared not stir until the eleventh.
